title: Butterfly release window chefbook and telemetry recipe (nov-2026 draft)
content:
TL;DR
A compact, low-traffic rollout pattern we're calling the 'Butterfly' window: small, elegant shifts that open and close quickly with staged telemetry gates. Use this for low-risk UX changes, small model variant switches, and config flips that should not require full blue/green. This doc is the working chefbook (recipes + snippets) and the release notes draft for customers.

Goals and constraints
- Keep user-visible impact minimal (target <0.1% error surface)
- Guaranteed automatic rollback on SLO breach at any gate
- Two-hour total window from first traffic increment to finish (typical)
- Observability-first: each step has a nominated dashboard and an enforcement query

Butterfly concept overview
- Phase 0: Preheat (prep only, no traffic)
- Phase 1: Petal (1% traffic for 10m)
- Phase 2: Flourish (5% traffic for 20m)
- Phase 3: Full-wing (20% traffic for 30m)
- Phase 4: Fold (ramp to target or revert)
Notes: each phase has automatic gates. If any gate trips, instant fallback to previous stable model/version and notify on-call.

Preflight checklist (owners in parentheses)
- Code & infra
  - Ensure PRs merged and deployment artifact built (owner: Eng-Release)
  - Tag image: registry.redwood.ai/release/<tag> (owner: CI Eng)
  - Verify infra defaults: rate limits, request timeouts, instance autoscaling policies (owner: Platform Eng)
- Tests
  - Smoke tests: /smoke/quick (success 3/3) (owner: QA)
  - Canary synthetic: run 1k synthetic samples against model variant B and compare latency and perplexity delta (owner: Applied ML)
- Observability
  - Nightwatch dashboard pinned: /dashboards/nightwatch/butterfly-<tag> (owner: Observability)
  - SLOs to watch: token-latency P95 < 600ms, error-rate < 0.2% (owner: SRE)
  - Alert routing: ensure #pager and #release-ops subscriptions are correct (owner: SRE)
- Communications
  - Post preflight note to #release-ops with go/no-go slack check (owner: Release Lead)
  - Email stakeholder list (product, concerns) with short summary (owner: Release Lead)

Traffic choreography (planner)
- Day: 2026-11-10 UTC (example)
- 10:00 UTC: Phase 0 start (prep, no traffic)
- 10:15 UTC: Phase 1 Petal -> route 1% to variant-B (10 minutes soak)
- 10:25 UTC: Evaluate gates (automated queries + one manual check)
- 10:35 UTC: Phase 2 Flourish -> 5% for 20 minutes
- 10:55 UTC: Gate evaluation & decision (auto-pass or rollback)
- 11:05 UTC: Phase 3 Full-wing -> 20% for 30 minutes
- 11:35 UTC: Final acceptance or rollback -> target traffic or revert
- 11:40 UTC: Fold (if accepted, route to target permanently; if reverted, begin postmortem)
Quick notes: keep a 5-minute breathing room between phases for emergency rollback.

Gates & enforcement queries (examples)
- Latency gate: p95(token_latency) by route over 5m windows <= 600ms OR fail
- Error gate: rate(errors) / rate(requests) over 5m <= 0.2% OR fail
- Quality gate (model): compare BLEU/perplexity for sample set; delta <= 1.5x baseline OR fail
- Cost gate: avg tokens-per-request not > 1.2x baseline over 15m OR warn
Snippets (promql-like)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/api/v1/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le))
- error rate: sum(increase(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total[5m]))

Rollback ladder (criteria + actions)
- Auto-rollback triggers (immediate):
  - latency gate fail -> immediate traffic shift to previous variant and page SRE
  - error gate fail -> immediate traffic shift and open incident channel
- Manual rollback triggers (investigation first):
  - quality gate marginal fail (between warn and fail) -> pause and run extended synthetic suite
  - cost gate exceeded -> consider throttling or QC review
Actions on rollback:
- Toggle routing switch: internal command (ops runbook) by Release Lead or SRE
- Post to #release-ops: 'ROLLBACK: <tag> -> <previous-tag> reason=<gate>'
- Attach preflight artifacts (smoke logs, synthetic run output, perf snapshots)

Operator quick commands (notes to self)
- kubectl: kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference runtime=registry.redwood.ai/release/<tag> --record
- terraform: terraform apply -var='canary_percent=5' -target=module.routing
- rollout-check: ./tools/check-rollout --env=prod --tag=<tag>

Smoke and post-release forensic captures
- Capture one-hour flamegraphs from STATSD, sample 200 traces from request_id header and archive to S3://release-artifacts/<tag>/traces
- Save KV-cache hit rates snapshot: query: avg(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) by(instance)
- Save model KV sizes and memory map snapshot (applied-ml script)

Release notes draft (customer-facing)
- headline: Improved model routing and smaller memory footprint for many inference paths
- items:
  - Reduced median token latency for conversational outlines by ~12% (internal A/B)
  - Tuned batching heuristics to avoid tail latencies during short bursts
  - Fixed edge-case where prompt embeddings could occasionally timeout under high concurrency
- Caveat: this rollout is incremental; expect the change to show for a small subset of traffic during the window. If you see regressions, please report to support@redwood.ai with request-id and timestamp.

Post-release follow-ups (owners and timelines)
- +24h: Run extended synthetic job (owner: Applied ML) -> compare long-tail metrics and quality on full dataset
- +48h: Cost sampling and billing delta analysis (owner: Finance Eng)
- +72h: Retro doc with timeline and signal snapshots (owner: Release Lead)

Open questions / notes to self
- Should we add a micro-canary step at 0.5% for high-risk customers on Dedicated clusters? (ask Sales/CS)
- Confirm if KMS rotation window overlaps with this deployment (Security)
- Consider automating the PromQL gate evaluation and making it first-class in the release API (product/infra)

Appendix A: Emergency contact ladder
- Primary SRE on-call: +1-555-101-020 (Slack: @rowan)
- Secondary Release Lead: Miguel Rivera (Slack: @miguel.r)
- Applied ML contact: Aisha Patel (Slack: @aisha)

Appendix B: Quick postmortem template
- What happened (one line)
- Timeline (minute-granular)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Actions taken during rollout
- Follow-ups and owners

Notes: this is a working draft. Keep feedback inline and add short snippets (commands/queries) rather than large copies of dashboards. If we accept the Butterfly pattern, we should codify the phase gates into release-ops automation by Q1 2027.
